questions.prompt: You're writing a short story (not a dialogue tree). One of your characters has a strong voice register. How does dialogue craft show up in the prose?

options.label: The character's dialogue lines stay in their register; the tag and action beats around them don't make the character sound like everyone else.
Drop dialogue entirely and use narration for everything.
Make every character sound the same so the prose flows smoothly.

questions.mentorPostScript: Voice register holds wherever the character speaks — dialogue tree, short story, comic panel.

questions.prompt: You're writing a comic strip. Three panels, three speech bubbles. What does branching-meaningfulness look like there?

options.label: Each panel's bubble makes a choice the reader can feel — what gets said vs what doesn't. The branches live in the gaps between panels.
Comics don't have branches because the reader doesn't choose.
Branches only matter in interactive fiction.

questions.mentorPostScript: Every choice a character makes is a branch. The reader feels the path NOT taken too.

questions.prompt: You're writing a poem with two voices alternating. How does subtext show up?

options.label: What one voice says out loud is contradicted, completed, or twisted by the other voice's line — the layer underneath the page-surface words.
Subtext only happens in dialogue trees.
Poems don't carry subtext because they're short.

questions.mentorPostScript: Subtext is the gap between what someone says and what they mean. It works in any form.

questions.prompt: You're writing a play script. Tag balance feels different there because plays use stage directions instead of attribution. What's the equivalent craft move?

options.label: Use stage directions sparingly — when an action beat (a pause, a gesture, an exit) carries information the dialogue can't say.
Use stage directions for every line so the reader knows exactly what's happening.
Never use stage directions because they break the dialogue's rhythm.

questions.mentorPostScript: Stage directions are the play's action beats. Use them where words can't carry the moment.

questions.prompt: Across every form (dialogue tree / short story / comic / poem / play script), what's the one craft move that travels with you?

options.label: Every line a character speaks is a choice. The choice carries voice + subtext + branch + tag. The form changes; the choice doesn't.
Use the same dialogue tag style in every form.
Pick one form and stick with it forever.

questions.mentorPostScript: Forms change. The craft of one line at a time stays the same. Patter is grinning.
